label: Cut-up line (wing separation)
description: The first and most important mixing point. Wings are cut from the carcass and drop onto a shared conveyor. A bird's left and right wing part company here and, in a commodity plant, never meet again.

label: Picking tray
description: Flowers are carried from the field and the three stigmas plucked out by hand into a shared tray. This is saffron's cut-up line: the first and most complete mixing event, and it happens within seconds of separation.

label: Wing chiller
description: Bulk immersion or air chilling. Thousands of wings tumble together in a single vessel with a residence time measured in tens of minutes.

label: Drying batch
description: A day's picking is dried together in one batch, sun or low heat. Several pickers' trays combine here, so the pool grows by roughly the size of the crew.

label: Size grading (jumbo / large / medium)
description: Wings are weighed individually and routed to grade streams. This is ACTIVE SEPARATION, not shuffling: a bird's two wings go to different boxes whenever they fall on opposite sides of a grade boundary. The single strongest driver pushing the answer toward 12.

label: Grade separation
description: Threads are sorted by grade, with the yellow style cut from the red stigma for the higher grades. Like wing size grading, this does not merely commingle - it actively separates a single flower's stigmas from one another when they are not identical, and they rarely are.

label: Combo bin
description: Bulk container, commonly around 2,000 lb. At roughly 0.23 lb per whole wing that is about 8,700 wings in one bin.

label: Lot packing
description: Graded threads are blended into commercial lots and filled into the small jars and packets sold at retail. A half-gram packet is drawn from a pool measured in kilograms.

label: IQF freezer tunnel
description: Individually quick frozen on a continuous belt. Continuous flow means no lot boundaries are preserved through this step.

label: Case pack
description: Boxed, commonly 40 lb - roughly 175 wings. Packing does not mix; it draws from an already-mixed stream. By this point essentially every wing in the case is from a different bird.

label: Distributor warehouse
description: Pallets assembled from many lots, plants, and sometimes producers.

label: Restaurant freezer bin
description: The bin is topped up from multiple cases across multiple deliveries. Old and new stock commingle - the practical reason a single order can span weeks of production.

label: Fryer basket
description: The draw itself. Twelve wings are scooped from the bin - the point at which the question finally gets answered.

label: Nest and belt collection
description: Hens lay into nest boxes and the eggs roll onto a conveyor shared by the whole house. This is where commingling begins - the direct counterpart of the cut-up line for wings - except that nothing is being separated, only gathered.

label: On-farm cooler
description: Eggs are cooled and held before processing. A day's lay from the whole house sits together, which is what makes a "same-day" carton a meaningful category at all.

label: Washing
description: US eggs are washed, which removes the cuticle and is why they are refrigerated afterwards. Eggs from many hens pass through the same line in continuous flow.

label: Candling and grading
description: Eggs are lit from below to find blood spots, meat spots and cracks, then sorted by weight into size classes. Unlike wing grading this splits nothing apart, because each egg was already a separate contribution from a separate hen.

label: Carton pack
description: Twelve eggs are placed in a carton. The draw itself, and the point at which the question gets answered - by now every egg in the carton is from a different hen.

label: Distributor
description: Cartons are palletised across farms and sometimes across producers. Irrelevant to the count, because the carton was sealed upstream - but it is why the carton in your hand cannot be traced to a house by looking at it.

label: Retail case
description: The shelf. Cartons from several lots sit side by side, and you pick one.

label: Your fridge
description: Where the carton finally sits. Included so the chain ends where the question does.
